transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm really embarrassed to be here, but I've been struggling with episodes where I completely lose control and eat massive amounts of food in a very short time. This has been happening for about seven months now, and I just don't know how to stop it.
After these episodes of overeating, do you engage in any behaviors to try to prevent weight gain, such as self-induced vomiting, misusing laxatives, or excessive exercising?

Yes, I'm so ashamed to admit it, but I usually force myself to throw up right after and take laxatives to get it out of my system. I also force myself to exercise for hours because I'm absolutely terrified of gaining weight.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [Binge-Eating Disorder, Bulimia Nervosa]. The patient confirmed engaging in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, and excessive exercise following binge episodes. These behaviors are the diagnostic criteria that distinguish Bulimia Nervosa from Binge-Eating Disorder. Therefore, Binge-Eating Disorder has been removed.
